text:
Lina: Heads up 7: compare table variant request. PM wants a denser view for power users: collapse meta into a hover reveal to show more rows per viewport. Thoughts on discoverability vs density?

Noah: Density is useful but we lose scannability. Could we provide a toggle: Compact / Comfortable with the compact mode hiding description + model tags and showing just name, version, and two badges? Add a small info tooltip when toggled: "Compact mode hides non-essential fields to show more rows".

Priya: Copy consistency: the catalog header currently reads "Models" but in compact mode it should read "Models (Compact)" so users know they changed the density. Also ensure keyboard toggling is possible via a dedicated button with aria-pressed state.

Anya: Implementation nuance: compact mode removes some DOM nodes; ensure live regions don't trigger unnecessarily. For the badges we discussed previously, keep the +N behaviour. Also consider sticky column for the model name so horizontal scroll doesn't lose context.

Noah: Also: in compact mode reduce badge size from 12px to 10px to increase density, but that may impact legibility. Jorge, any color/contrast guidance?

Jorge: 10px icons are risky. If we must shrink, increase weight/contrast to maintain AA. For the compact label, add an aria-label with the full name (e.g., "Model: Llama-2-7B, version 1.2.3") so screen readers have the same context even when visual elements are hidden.

Lina: I'm going to mock a compact toggle and show both modes in the design doc. Prioritize accessibility props and the compact header copy change.

design-bot: Compact/comfortable mock uploaded: https://www.figma.com/file/.../catalog-compact-toggle  comments enabled for @Lina @Noah @Priya.

Lina: Quick decision: ship the toggle behind a feature flag and do a small user test with 5 internal folks. If no major issues, enable for power users next release.

Priya: LGTM. Also add a telemetry flag for "compact_toggle_used" to see uptake.

Noah: I'll scope frontend changes: CSS variable for density, compact class that hides nodes, and keep DOM accessible labels.

Anya: I'll sync the microcopy updates too. Thanks team.
